keyA.notes: p.057 continues p.056's last sentence ('وَأَعْظِم لِي نُورًا،' then 'وَأَعْطِنِي نُورًا'), so it gets '+'; p.059 and p.060 also continue mid-sentence ('+'); p.058 starts the new section (# heading per STRUCTURE). No footnote continues across pages. Bold: the phrases in bold type (parenthesised Mashishiyya text) are wrapped as (**…**) and «**…**», with the parentheses and quotes outside the markers. This follows keyA b17 for this section, and the quote marks visibly use the light weight. On p.059 only (وَتَنَزَّلَتْ عُلُومُ آدَمَ) is bold; the other parenthesised phrases there are set in the regular weight and are not marked. The line «(تُقْرَأُ مَرَّة يوميًّا …)» under the heading is printed bold but is written as a plain paragraph per STRUCTURE §2. In 'ب«كُنْتُ' the tatweel after the ba is dropped. The name الله with a printed case vowel but with the font's automatic shadda/alif ligature is written بِاللهِ / اللهُ, as in keyA b14. Quran: dagger alif written directly after the letter; the round silent-alif sign (shape checked against the khaa-head sukun) is ۟ in ظَّلَمُوٓا۟ / فَٱسْتَغْفَرُوا۟ / لَوَجَدُوا۟; the waqf ۚ after تَعْلَمُ is written with a space; فَٱتَّبِعُونِى ends in a dotless ى as printed. Many overlapping marks over 'الْمـ' clusters were resolved by connected-component analysis of 1600-2400 dpi renders: regular-font sukun+fatha (الْمَمْدُودِ، الْمَلَكُوتِ، الْجَبَرُوتِ، الْمَوْسُوطُ); sukun+damma (الْمُمْكِنَةُ، الْمُتَلَأْلِئَةِ (+ta fatha merged in)، الْمُزَكَّى (+zay fatha merged in)، الْمُؤَيَّدُ، الْمُوْصُوفَةُ). In the bold font, sukun is a circle, and the 'hat' shape (circle crossed by a fatha) = sukun+fatha (وَالْجَسَدِ، الْحَقَائِقُ، الْجَامِعُ). Words whose lam/mim carries only a damma with an open loop are written without a sukun on the lam (المُتَوَّجِ، المُودَعَةُ، المُشِعَّةُ). validate.py prints OK with one warning: on p.059 the footnote ref (١) is glued after the closing ﴾ ('(١١٣)﴾(١)'), as printed, and the validator does not count it.

In the bold lam-alif the fatha sits over the lam stroke and nothing stands over the hamza (compare الْأَسْرَارُ / الْأَبَدِ on the same page, where the hamza's fatha is directly above the hamza and the lam carries a sukun). Expected الْأَنْوَارُ. Checked at 5000 dpi. Kept as printed.
Three kasras are printed: under the د, under the dots of the ي, and under the final ه (expected تَهْدِيهِ). Checked at 3200 dpi. Kept as printed.
The lam-alif of إلا has only a fatha and no shadda (expected إِلَّا). Checked at 2000 dpi. Kept as printed.
إلا is printed with the kasra under the hamza but no shadda/fatha on the lam-alif (expected إِلَّا; إِلَّا لَهُ two lines earlier has the shadda). Kept as printed.

keyB.notes: Markers: p057 '+' because p056 ends mid-sentence («وَأَعْظِم لي نُورًا،») and p057 begins «وَأَعْطِنِي نُورًا»; p056 has no footnotes, so no (تابع). p058 opens the new section with the # heading (no '+'). p059 '+' (continues «(وَفِيهِ ارْتَقَتِ الْحَقَائِقُ)» → «الْمُمْكِنَةُ…»); p060 '+' (continues «(لَذَهَبَ كَمَا» → «قِيلَ الْمَوْسُوطُ)»). The line under the heading «(تُقْرَأُ مَرَّة يوميًّا…)» is printed bold but is written as a plain paragraph per STRUCTURE §2; tatweel in «يـوم»، «الجمعـة» dropped. Bold vs regular was decided by measuring median stroke width at 1200 dpi (bold ≈16-18 px, regular ≈11-13 px): bold = (اللَّهُمَّ صلِّ)، (عَلَى)، (مَنْ مِنْهُ انْشَقَّتِ الْأَسْرَارُ)، «كُنْتُ نَبِيًّا وَآدَمُ بَيْنَ الرُّوحِ وَالْجَسَدِ» (the guillemets themselves are regular weight, so ** is inside them)، (وَانْفَلَقَتِ الَأنْوَارُ)، (وَفِيهِ ارْتَقَتِ الْحَقَائِقُ) on p058; only (وَتَنَزَّلَتْ عُلُومُ آدَمَ) on p059 (all the other parenthesised Mashishiya phrases on p059 measure regular); on p060 (صَلَاةً)، (تَلِيقُ بِكَ)، (مِّنْكَ)، (إِلَيْهِ)، (كَمَا هُوَ أَهْلُهُ. اللَّهُمَّ إِنَّهُ سِرُّكَ الْجَامِعُ)، (الدَّالُّ)، (عَلَيْكَ)، (وَحِجَابُكَ الْأَعْظَمُ الْقَائِمُ لَكَ) — parentheses included in the ** as in keyB b17. Lam ligatures (لم، لج، لح، لخ) were checked at 3600-7000 dpi: the lam's mark and (for لم) the mim's mark sit together at the ligature top, the next letter's mark sits lower-left; a sukun+fatha or sukun+damma pair overlapping at the top can look like a single damma at normal zoom (bold: circle-sukun crossed by a fatha). This resolves الْمَمْدُودِ، وَالْجَسَدِ، الْحَقَائِقُ (p058), الْمُمْكِنَةُ، الْمَلَكُوتِ (p059), الْمَوْسُوطُ، الْجَامِعُ، الْمُزَكَّى، الْمُؤَيَّدُ (p060) as written; المُودَعَةُ، المُتوَّجِ، المُشِعَّةُ carry only the mim's damma (no lam sukun). p058 «بـ«كُنْتُ»: the joining tatweel after ب is dropped (validator rule), giving «ب«». Reference ranges are written in logical order with an ASCII hyphen and no spaces: [الأحزاب: ٤٥-٤٦] (printed «٤٥ -٤٦») and [المائدة: ١٥-١٦] (printed «١٥ - ١٦»). The footnote mark (١) on p059 follows the closing ﴾ directly (﴾(١) [النساء: ١١٣]), so validate.py cannot see it and warns 'footnote refs [2, 3] vs [1, 2, 3]'; the mark is printed there. Quran: all nine quotations match Tanzil letter-for-letter (dagger alif without tatweel; madda written ا+ٓ; silent alif ۟; small waw/yeh ۥ ۦ; waqf ۚ after تَعْلَمُ in النساء ١١٣ as printed; لَعَلَىٰ with its printed dagger alif). The word Allah in ordinary text is written with only its printed case vowel (بِالله، اللهُ، وَاللهُ) as in earlier keyB batches. Final ى with the Lotus automatic small alif is written plain (أَحْصَى، عَلَى، حَتَّى، فَتَجَلَّى، تُزْجَى، الْمُزَكَّى، وَصَلَّى). Partial vowelling kept as printed, e.g. صلِّ (no fatha on ص), وَاجْعَل لِّي، شَيءٍ (p057, no sukun) vs شَيْءٍ (p059), كَثِيْرًا (sukun on madd ي), والنُّعُوتِ (bare و), وَجَدتُّ (bare د), مِن رَّفِيعِ. Honorifics in footnotes are printed as words (رضي الله عنه، عليه السلام) and kept so; ﷺ on p059 kept as glyph. Zoom images: scratch\b15B\.
